title: When the Garden Wakes
premise: Edmund Galloway, the last swordspeaker bound by an oath that keeps him in a valley where magic cannot follow, has spent thirty years tending a garden and forgetting his past. When a child named Wren arrives speaking the dead tongue of Aldermere — a kingdom erased from every map and memory but his — Edmund learns the long winter falling on the world is the dying breath of that vanished country, and only a swordspeaker can open the door out of it. Dragged back into magic he swore away, Edmund must choose between the oath that keeps him safe and hollow and the duty of returning a lost child to a home that no longer exists. In the end, Edmund breaks his oath to speak the door open, sacrificing his own place in the unmagicked valley so Wren can pass through; the garden wakes around him as winter lifts, and he steps into a world remade, belonging nowhere and finally free.
about_author: Ines Halloran is a former botanist who left fieldwork to write fantasy rooted in folklore of forgotten places. She lives at the edge of a national forest, where she keeps an unruly garden and claims the birds gossip in languages she almost understands.

chapters.title: The Child at the Gate
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. On the first frost of autumn, a mud-streaked child appears at Edmund's gate speaking Aldermere's dead tongue — words Edmund hasn't heard since the kingdom fell. He takes her in against every instinct, recognizing in her speech the oath-marks of his own order. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness cracking open thirty years of deliberate stillness.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Edmund and Wren. Magic cannot cross the valley's border, but Wren is fading anyway — the erased country is pulling its last speakers back into the long winter. Edmund tests the valley's edge and finds his old sword humming beyond the boundary stones. Emotional beat: dread and dawning responsibility as safety proves to be a slow kind of death.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Aldermere
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, with Edmund alongside. Following fragments of the dead tongue, they journey to the ruins where Aldermere's final door stands guarded by the Hollow Court — oath-breakers corrupted by the power they once served. Edmund must duel his former mentor, now the Court's voice, who offers him restoration if he abandons the child. Emotional beat: climax of love against duty as Edmund refuses and shatters his oath to speak the door open.

chapters.title: When the Garden Wakes
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The door opens onto spring; Wren passes through to the remade Aldermere, but the broken oath bars Edmund from following or returning to the valley. Left in the threshold country, he plants the seeds he carried from his garden — and the ground answers, magic waking gently for the first time in his hands. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging, an ending that is an beginning.
